summary: Backend-only round-2 tests for the 4 new feature areas (attachments via Emergent Object Storage, patient timeline, 5 CSV exports, Twilio/WhatsApp reminder with graceful PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED fallback) + audit log verification. 20/20 new tests pass. Re-ran round-1 regression: 33/33 still pass.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1154 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, cases, attachments, exports, reminders, ai). Past the 700-line guideline.

Attachment upload reads full bytes into memory before the 10MB check. With many large uploads this risks worker RAM spikes; consider streaming/length-check via Content-Length header to short-circuit early.

send_whatsapp/send_sms use blocking `requests.post` inside async endpoints (_deliver_reminder). When real keys are configured this will block the event loop — switch to httpx.AsyncClient or run in a threadpool.
patient_timeline performs N+1 queries (per case: doctor, payment, notes, prescriptions, attachments_count). For patients with many cases this is slow — batch with $in or aggregation.
CSV exports load up to 100000 rows into memory via to_list before streaming — fine now, but for real growth use a Mongo cursor + streaming generator into StreamingResponse.

Attachment `storage_path` uses `result['path']` from put_object response without validating the contract; if storage returns an unexpected shape this raises KeyError 500. Add a defensive fallback to the constructed path.
Attachment delete is soft-delete only — orphan objects remain in Emergent Object Storage. Consider a background reaper or hard-delete option for admin.
